card.name: Halling
card.profile: Vigorous Norwegian men’s folk dance (bygdedans) of Hallingdal and Valdres; fast and acrobatic, often solo (laus), with leaps, spins and feats of strength. Signature move is the hallingkast — kicking a hat held high on a stick. Grieg composed halling pieces. NOT UNESCO.

observation.setting: Indoor stage with theatrical lighting, decorative screens, and musicians seated at the side, while a woman in folk dress stands elevated on a chair holding a long pole with a hat.
observation.dancers: One male solo dancer initially, later accompanied by a female dancer standing on a chair with a pole and hat
observation.formation_and_space: Solo dancer moving across the stage floor in various directions
observation.posture: Upright torso, slight knee bends, shifts in weight as the dancer moves
observation.footwork: Stepping, kicking, leaps, and turns on the balls and heels of the feet, synchronized with the music
observation.arms_and_hands: Arms held wide, crossed over chest, or gesturing, sometimes holding or interacting with a hat
observation.hips_and_torso: Torso twists and bends during jumps and turns
observation.levels_jumps_turns: Frequent high leaps, low crouches, jumps, spins, and headspins/floor rolls
observation.costume_and_props: Male dancer wears dark trousers, white sleeved shirt, red vest/waistcoat, neckerchief, and a dark hat. Female dancer wears a patterned traditional dress with an apron and a decorative cap, holding a long wooden pole with a hat attached to the end.
observation.cannot_infer: Exact footwork nuances and weight distribution details are difficult to determine due to camera angle shifts and distance.
